core_obligations: Reduce to one affine piece (proof lines 3155-3168): take the minimal number n of affine opens needed to cover X together with U; proving the statement for the case n = 1 allows one to extend the pair successively over the pieces, so one reduces to n = 1.

Reduce to an affine scheme (proof lines 3170-3180): if X = U union V with V affine, then the intersection of U and V is quasi-compact because X is quasi-separated; applying the statement on V to the restricted data and glueing the result to the given sheaf along the common restriction yields the statement for X, so one reduces to X affine.

Finish on an affine scheme (proof lines 3182-3222): by the trivial extension lemma there is a quasi-coherent H with a map psi to F restricting to the pair; by the extension lemma one replaces H by a finite type submodule with the same restriction, then identifies it with a module over the ring and chooses a surjection from a finite free module onto it; since G is finitely presented the kernel restricted to U is of finite type, so the extension lemma provides a finite type submodule K' of the kernel restricting to it, and the quotient of the finite free module by K' is the required finitely presented extension of G with the map induced by psi.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a cover by U and a single affine open, and then to an affine base by glueing.
On an affine scheme produce a quasi-coherent extension and shrink it to a finite type submodule.
Present the finite type module and control the kernel to obtain a finitely presented extension.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme X, a quasi-coherent module F, a quasi-compact open U and a finitely presented module G on U with a map to F restricted to U, there is a finitely presented module on X restricting to the given data (statement lines 3140-3153). The proof (proof lines 3155-3226) reduces to a single affine piece outside U and then to an affine base by glueing, produces a quasi-coherent extension there, shrinks it to a finite type submodule, presents it by a finite free module and controls the kernel to obtain a finitely presented extension. H3: a multi-step reduction with a genuine kernel argument at the end, written out in full.
